newsitem.title: USA: St. Paul Bancorp splits stock, raises dividend.
newsitem.headline: St. Paul Bancorp splits stock, raises dividend.

text.p: St. Paul Bancorp Inc said Friday it set a three-for-two split of outstanding shares, and also raised its quarterly cash dividend on a split-adjusted basis by 25 percent to $0.10 a share.

The new shares in the stock split will be distributed on July 14 to shareholders of record as of June 30. The increased dividend rate is to become effective on the declaration of the company's next quarterly dividend in mid-July, it added.

"This three-for-two stock split will enhance the liquidity of St. Paul Bancorp stock, making it more affordable to retail investors," Joseph Scully, chairman, said in a statement. "Furthermore, the increase in the cash dividend rate reflects the board's continued confidence in St. Paul Bancorp's performance and enhances the stock's return to shareholders."
St. Paul Bancorp is parent of St. Paul Federal Bank for Savings.
